You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Seagate Technology Fiscal Q4 2026 Earnings Highlights: Revenue of $3.63 Billion Up 48% Year-over-Year, Record Non-GAAP Gross Margin of 52.7%, Adjusted EPS of $5.71 Significantly Beats Expectations, Driven by Strong Data Center Growth

TEXT:
Core View
Seagate Technology ( NASDAQ : STX ) reported fiscal fourth-quarter (ended July 3, 2026) and full-year 2026 results that exceeded expectations on both revenue and non-GAAP earnings per share, with gross margin and operating margin reaching record highs. Q4 revenue was $3.629 billion, up 48% year-over-year and 17% sequentially. Non-GAAP diluted EPS reached $5.71, up 121% year-over-year. Full-year revenue totaled $12.195 billion, up 34%, with non-GAAP EPS of $15.58 and record free cash flow of $3.105 billion. Performance was primarily driven by robust cloud data center demand and strong execution on HAMR technology.
The company provided strong guidance for fiscal Q1 2027, expecting revenue of $4.1 billion (±$100 million) and non-GAAP EPS of $7.30 (±$0.20). Shares closed down approximately 8.53% on the day, with some recovery in after-hours trading following the beat.
Detailed Breakdown
Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
Q4 revenue: $3.629 billion, up 48% year-over-year (from $2.444 billion) and 17% sequentially (from $3.112 billion), above the midpoint of guidance.
GAAP gross margin: 52.3%; non-GAAP gross margin: 52.7% (record high), up 570 basis points sequentially and 1,480 basis points year-over-year.
Non-GAAP operating margin: 44.6% (record), up 710 basis points sequentially and 1,840 basis points year-over-year; GAAP operating margin: 43.0%.
Non-GAAP net income: $1.319 billion; GAAP net income: $1.294 billion.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS: $5.71 (up 121% year-over-year from $2.59); GAAP diluted EPS: $5.58 (from $2.24), both well above Wall Street consensus of approximately $5.10.
Cash flow from operations: $1.305 billion; free cash flow: $1.118 billion (up 163% year-over-year).
Full year: Revenue $12.195 billion (up 34% from $9.097 billion); non-GAAP gross margin 46.1%, GAAP 45.6%; non-GAAP operating margin 36.5%; non-GAAP EPS $15.58 (up approximately 92%); GAAP EPS $13.90; operating cash flow $3.674 billion; free cash flow $3.105 billion (record); retired $1.4 billion in debt and returned $810 million to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases.
Data Center Business Performance
Data center revenue: $2.933 billion, up 57% year-over-year, representing approximately 81% of total revenue.
Nearline (data center) exabyte shipments: 195 EB, up 43% year-over-year and 11% sequentially.
Total hard drive shipments: 218 EB, up 34% year-over-year; approximately 90% shipped into data center markets.
Cloud customers achieved three consecutive years of sequential quarterly exabyte growth; enterprise/OEM data center markets delivered double-digit year-over-year growth in both revenue and exabyte shipments.
HAMR products accounted for approximately 40% of nearline exabyte shipments; Mozaic 3+ is qualified and in volume production with all major cloud customers, while Mozaic 4+ is ramping with the two largest global CSPs.
Key drivers: Sustained demand for mass-capacity storage fueled by AI-accelerated data generation, combined with the company’s pricing discipline and operational execution.
Other Business Segments Performance
Edge IoT revenue: $697 million, up 20% year-over-year and 14% sequentially, representing approximately 19% of total revenue.
Non-nearline shipments: 23 EB, down 10% year-over-year.
Business mix continues to shift toward data center, with Edge IoT’s share declining from 24% in the year-ago quarter to 19%.
Future Plans and Capital Structure
Technology roadmap: Mozaic 4+ (supporting up to ~44 TB) is expected to represent the majority of HAMR shipments by the end of calendar 2026; Mozaic 5+ (higher density) is on track for qualification shipments starting in late calendar 2027. Nearline capacity is largely allocated through calendar 2028, with customers extending planning horizons into 2029 and beyond.
Debt and shareholder returns: Retired $302 million of debt in Q4 and returned $283 million to shareholders; for the full year, retired $1.4 billion of debt, reduced net debt to approximately $1.9 billion, and improved net leverage to 0.4x. Plans to further retire high-yield notes and convertible notes, targeting gross debt of roughly $2.4 billion by the end of fiscal Q1 2027.
Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $1.704 billion; total liquidity of approximately $3.0 billion (including undrawn revolving credit facility).
Capital expenditures expected to remain in the 4%–6% of revenue range, focused on supporting HAMR capacity and technology advancement.
Fiscal Q1 2027 Guidance
Revenue: $4.1 billion (±$100 million).
Non-GAAP diluted EPS: $7.30 (±$0.20).
Non-GAAP operating expenses: approximately $300 million; non-GAAP operating margin expected at approximately 50% at the revenue midpoint.
Non-GAAP tax rate: approximately 16%; diluted share count: approximately 231 million (including ~2 million shares of estimated dilution from the 2028 Exchangeable Senior Notes).
Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth to exceed the 34% recorded in fiscal 2026, with sequential improvement in revenue, margins, and cash generation throughout the year.
Market Context and Investor Concerns
Core drivers: Persistent structural demand for high-capacity, cost-efficient storage from AI workloads and cloud data centers, with Seagate benefiting from its HAMR/Mozaic platform advantages in both volume and pricing. High visibility from capacity allocations provides additional confidence.
Potential concerns: Shares had risen sharply prior to the report, raising valuation sensitivity; the approximately 8.53% intraday decline reflected some profit-taking and broader market sen time nt. Longer-term monitoring points include the pace of HAMR ramp execution, competitive dynamics, pricing sustainability, and potential macroeconomic impacts on enterprise IT spending.
Management reiterated that momentum is expected to continue into 2027, supported by durable long-term demand for mass-capacity storage as AI increases both the volume and value of data.
